Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered
- Primary goals: reduce inference latency for interactive UX (target p95 <100ms), predictable tail latency, and lower per-token cost for your multi-tenant product.
- Current comparison set: your self-hosted experiments, AWS Bedrock, and a quick Redwood Dedicated eval.
- Constraints: 512 token input + ~64 token output, 8 concurrent sessions (simulating product load).

Action items we agreed
1) Redwood to share the initial benchmark numbers we ran during the call + a short plan for the A/B tests we recommend. (David/DSE will send artifacts)
2) Globex to confirm the set of in-house prompts you want us to run for the A/B (narrowed to 12 prompts).
3) Schedule a short follow-up to review the numbers and pick the PoC approach — propose Tue 3/23 10:00am PT.

Attachments: I’ll share David’s CSV with raw runs and a 1-page summary.

If that matches your read, I’ll book the 3/23 slot and loop in our infra engineer to run the deeper A/B.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks + next steps

Alice / team — attaching the raw CSV and a short PDF summary as promised. Quick notes on methodology and the headline numbers below.

Methodology (short)- Model: open-variant LLM v1 (architecture matched across runs)- Input profile: 512 tokens in, 64 tokens out (deterministic prompts)- Concurrency: 8 parallel clients- Requests: 10,000 per config (warmup 1,000 discarded)- Batching: disabled for p95/p99 latency runs (we measure single-request tail behavior). For throughput tokens/sec we ran batching-friendly config (small batch size 4) to reflect production mode.

Headline numbers (median / p95 / p99 / tokens/sec)- Redwood Dedicated (quantized 8-bit, GPU optimized kernels): median 28 ms / p95 42 ms / p99 78 ms / tokens/sec 220- Redwood Hosted API (shared capacity, autoscaled, same optimizations but multi-tenant noise): median 40 ms / p95 60 ms / p99 120 ms / tokens/sec 150- AWS Bedrock (our replicate on comparable instance): median 62 ms / p95 85 ms / p99 180 ms / tokens/sec 110

Interpretation- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Reserved) gives materially lower tail latency and higher tokens/sec vs both Hosted and Bedrock in these tests.- Difference between p95 and p99 indicates tail behavior under occasional KV cache misses and longer attention kernels; we can improve p99 via kernel tuning + KV caching for long histories.

Next tests we recommend (A/B plan)
1) Run your Bedrock A/B with the exact 12 prompts and same concurrency; we’ll coordinate to ensure identical scheduling.
2) Redwood will run two additional configs: (A) 4-bit quantization + kernel tuning (expect ~1.3-1.6x tokens/sec uplift), (B) KV cache priming test to measure effect for repeated prompt prefixes.
3) Measure both latency (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec at 5 loads: concurrency [1,4,8,16,32].

Practical ask
- Can you provision a short test window on your Bedrock account on Mon 3/22 or Tue 3/23? We’d like overlapping runs to reduce time skew.
- Confirm the 12 prompts file (I attached prompts_sample.csv) and whether sampling/random seeds should be fixed.

Attachments: globex_benchmarks_20260321.csv (raw runs), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf (one-pager).

Cheers,
David Kim
Senior SRE, Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference
